newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee may see cooler temps to July - Somar.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee may see cooler temps to July - Somar.

text.p: The north of Brazil's Sao Paulo state and southern Minas Gerais may see below average temperatures in May through to July, said independent forecasters Somar in a monthly bulletin.
"This is due to the entry of cold air masses, which, together with clear skies (common in winter), favors low temperatures in the early mornings," Somar said.
The north of Sao Paulo state and south Minas Gerais are two of Brazil's key coffee regions.

Rainfall throughout the southeastern region should be mainly around average for the time of year, except for the center and west of Minas Gerais where there should be slightly higher rainfall than usual.
Rains in April have been below average throughout most of the southeast with the exception of a small area in central Minas Gerais state where rains were more plentiful than usual.

In the south, east and north of Sao Paulo, the Cerrado and Zona da Mata regions of Minas Gerais and Espirito Santo, rains were between 25 and 70 millimeters below expectations for the month, Somar said.
"This means that the dry period in the southeast (winter) has already begun with a water deficit," Somar said.
In north Parana, rainfall should be normal during May to July while temperatures should be slightly above average.
In the bulletin Somar also mentioned signs of the return of the El Nino weather phenomenon.

"But even with the possible El Nino configuration, it is important to remember that its consequences in South America are not immediate. As far as the climate is concerned, this phenomenon affects rainfall and temperatures only from next summer," Somar said. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
